goal: A thesis author can build real editable OMML, Word fields, footnotes, sections, headers, footers and page-number structures from Compiler-resolved semantics and template policy.
non_goals: Do not change Markdown syntax, Parser behavior or Domain Model Word neutrality.
Do not change Template Model fields or template YAML schema.
Do not implement bibliography loading or citation formatting before task 006.
Do not implement temporary output or atomic replacement before task 007.
Do not add UI, network, account or AI dependencies.
Do not claim support for LaTeX outside the documented V1 subset.
expected_evidence: Observed RED and GREEN math, Compiler and DOCX XML tests
Documented renderer-neutral MathConverter contract and supported LaTeX subset
Direct editable OMML and equation bookmark XML assertions
Direct complex SEQ, REF, TOC, PAGE and NUMPAGES field assertions
Direct footnotes package part, content type, relationship, definition and reference assertions
Direct multiple-section, header/footer relationship and page-number format/restart assertions
Full pytest, Ruff and pip check output
Offline example build, package inspection, reload and LibreOffice conversion
Task report, independent spec review and independent quality review
unsafe_assumptions: python-docx high-level APIs do not cover every required advanced Word structure.
Renderer must not parse Markdown or LaTeX semantics, calculate numbers, resolve references or generate bookmark names.
Visible static text is not evidence of a real Word field, OMML object, footnote or section relationship.
Unsupported LaTeX must fail explicitly rather than degrade to text, image or partial XML.
Word, WPS and LibreOffice may differ in field update behavior, so update-on-open and package structure require direct tests.
stop_condition: Stop if implementation crosses Parser or Domain boundaries, requires bibliography or atomic-output behavior, edits outside allowed files, simulates Word objects, or lacks direct XML evidence.
